chapters.teaser: The habit everyone's noticed and nobody's mentioned.

chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Byeong, you don't enter a room, you happen to it. Ten seconds in, people know your name, your opinion on the playlist, and that you're the fun one. You're warm, generous, a little loud, and genuinely delightful. People feel seen by you, which is your real magic. What they also clock: you need an audience. Not in a bad way. You just light up when people are watching and dim slightly when they're not. That isn't vanity. That's a sun noticing it's daytime. Still, it's worth knowing that everyone can tell when you're on.
text.your-red-flag: Red flag, Byeong: you overshare, overcommit and overexplain, all before lunch. You say yes to every plan because you love people, then cancel two of them because you're exhausted. You're honest to the point of did you really have to say that at the table. And when you're hurt, you don't hide it. The whole room gets the weather report, with satellite images. Openness is lovely. A little filter is also lovely. You're allowed to have both. They're not mutually exclusive, no matter what your mouth has been telling you.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: With someone you love, you go big and fast. Grand gestures, enormous feelings, a shared playlist by week two. Partners feel like they're in a film and then start wondering when the credits roll. Your sabotage is burning hot and getting bored, or falling for people who are cool and distant because the chase is fun. Spoiler: a cold person doesn't warm up because you shine harder. They just get a tan. Try someone who's warm back. It will feel less exciting at first. It will also feel like being loved, which is better.
text.friends-and-work: At work you're the energy. Brainstorms, team mood, the presentation everyone remembers for weeks. Follow-through? Let's discuss it. You start ten things and finish four, brilliantly. With friends you're the host, the hype person, the one who organizes everyone's birthday. But you can take it personally when people don't match your energy. Not everyone runs at your voltage. That's not rejection. That's just the difference between lamps and suns. Lamps are fine. Lamps are cozy. Let them be lamps without reading it as a review of you. And maybe hand the spreadsheet part to someone who enjoys it.
text.the-lie: The story you keep telling yourself: I'm fine, I'm always fine. You're the happy one, so you feel like you're not allowed a bad day. Wrong. You also tell yourself that being liked by everyone matters. It really doesn't. Being loved by a few matters, and those few want to see you on a cloudy day too. They're not booking you for the sunshine. They're booking you for you. Let them see the weather sometimes, without turning it into a show. Quietly sad is allowed. The people worth keeping will stay through a gray week. That's how you'll know who they are.
text.the-fix: The fix, because Bom is pouting. Finish one thing before you start the next. Pause three seconds before the honest comment and check whether it's kind as well as true. Schedule one evening a week with nothing in it: no plans, no audience, no content. In love, slow the first month down and look for someone who's warm, not someone you have to defrost. Your light is the best thing about you. Just stop spending all of it on other people's rooms. Save some for your own. There. Bom is beaming. Disgusting.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, you said yes to four plans tonight. It's Tuesday.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Loves people, then cancels by voice note. From the bath.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, a cold crush doesn't melt because you shine harder.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Agreed. Now pick someone who's warm back. Radical.

spring.intro: Spring Byeong, your season belonged to Wood and feeds your Fire, so you've got unlimited fuel and you use all of it. You're the friend who turns a quiet Tuesday into an event. People clock you as fun, loud and probably the one who suggested shots. Your red flag is optimism used as avoidance. Problem at work? It'll be fine. Friend upset? Let's go out. Relationship wobbling? Let's book a trip. You'd rather add sunshine than look at the crack. Bom loves that about you. I love it too, mostly. The fix: when something's wrong, sit with it for ten minutes before you try to cheer it up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Booking a weekend away is not how you fix an argument, Byeong.

summer.intro: Summer-born Byeong: Fire ran the season and doubled your element. You're the sun at noon, which means you're glorious and a little hard to look at directly. People know you're in the room before they see you. The red flag: everything is about the energy, and the energy is about you. You don't mean to make it your show. It just becomes your show. Friends tell a story, you tell a bigger one. In love you're passionate and then suddenly bored the second it gets ordinary. At work you start five projects and finish two. The fix: ask one follow-up question before you share your own story. Let someone else be the weather.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your friend got engaged and you told the story of your holiday. Byeong. Please.

autumn.intro: Autumn Byeong, you were born while Metal was in charge and Fire's job is to work Metal, so you're a sun with a to-do list. Warm, and also weirdly competitive. People see someone generous and capable. Your friends know you keep score: who planned the last dinner, who paid, who texted first. Your red flag is turning love into a project you can win. In relationships you try to fix your partner like a renovation. At work you'll take over a task because you'd do it better, and you might, but now everyone feels useless. The fix: let something be done badly by someone else. Clap anyway. That's real warmth.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've kept a mental tally of who paid for brunch since 2023. Byeong.

winter.intro: Winter Byeong, Water ran your birth season and Water puts out Fire. So you shine like someone who's had to fight for it, a little too bright and a little too fast. People see the life of the party. Your friends know you leave early, go home and lie on the floor. Your red flag is performing happiness so nobody sees you dim. You'll say you're great with your whole chest while running on empty. In love you hide the cold days until they become a cold month. At work you overcommit to look on top of it. The fix: tell one person you're tired and don't follow it with a joke.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be cloudy sometimes, Byeong. We still like you.

earth.intro: Earth days close every season, and you were born in them, Byeong. Fire feeds Earth, so your heat goes straight into other people's ground. You host, you cheer, you fix the mood. People see sunshine. Your friends see someone who never admits being tired. Your red flag is generosity with a hidden invoice. In love you give so much that you start keeping score in secret. At work you take on the morale of the whole team. The fix: say no to one favor this week, warmly, without a reason.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The sun doesn't send invoices, Byeong. Stop doing it in your head.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Byeong. Your sun is well fed, so you burn bright and loud, and frankly you take up a lot of oxygen. The blind spot: you don't notice when other people are dimming next to you. You finish their stories, top their news, fill every silence. You think you're bringing the energy. Some of them are just waiting for a turn. In love your partner can end up feeling like a backing dancer. The fix: in your next three conversations, talk less than half the time. Count if you have to. You'll learn things. Wild.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Byeong, so your sun runs on thin fuel and you keep it lit with approval. You're the life of the party who checks whether everyone liked you on the way home. The blind spot: people-pleasing in a fun costume. You agree to everything and laugh at every joke, then wonder why you're exhausted and lonely in a full room. In love you hide your bad moods to stay lovable. The fix: cancel one plan you don't want to go to. No dramatic excuse. Just can't tonight. You'll survive.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything feels urgent, out loud or only on the inside, and your feelings arrive with sirens on even when nobody else can hear them. You're bright company, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the color, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyze it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair color twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
